speed: n/a (locked frame; he comes to camera)
angle: level, lens right on the water surface
start_frame: Water-level from the curtain up the hall toward the glass table, the waterline cutting across the frame as an eye-line: the White Rabbit appearing out of the dark between the lamp pools, small and coming on.
end_frame: The same frame with him much nearer, bounding on all four legs through four inches of water — every foot displacing water, ripples starting under his own feet, wet fur to the elbow, the gloves and fan carried in his mouth.
constraint_honoured: 'Contact evidence is mandatory: every foot displaces water and the ripples begin where he touches' — a still lens on the surface is what makes that evidence photographic rather than asserted.
movement_note: The shot where the animal either works or does not; a camera move would add a second uncertainty on top of the water contact. His approach supplies all the motion.
